topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic welcomes the students and outlines the core learning objectives of the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: Surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional cancer interventions—including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapies—along with their associated systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeting cancer-specific dependencies and DNA repair vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule kinase inhibitors that target oncogenic driver alterations, detailing their therapeutic mechanisms, off-target effects, and pathways of acquired resistance.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic actions of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates used to target tumor cell-surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunosurveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and explore immunotherapies designed to activate or engineer T cells to eliminate malignant cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review overall progress in cancer survival rates, current treatment challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and emerging clinical and diagnostic directions for future cancer management.
